headline: Ocean-freight stress is HIGH and holding — 44.5/100; Cape of Good Hope is the lead driver, -22% vs normal

bullets.text: Global Ocean Freight Stress is **44.5/100** (**high**), flat week-over-week. 4 of 28 monitored chokepoints are disrupted.
The biggest driver is **Cape of Good Hope**, running **80.0/day** vs a normal of **103.0/day** (-22%).
**368** changes to the disruption set since the last update.
Also moving now: **Bab el-Mandeb Strait** is running **43% below** normal.
Market context: Brent crude **$109.51/bbl** (+3.19% prev_close) — context for the energy-route chokepoints, not a stated cause.
Against the loaded sample trade book, **$415.5M** routes through disrupted lanes — an estimated **$3.3M** cost-of-delay ($1.8M–$5.3M).
